lines: I.  Introduction

A design buys observations to certify the Top-k of a set of relations ranked by CAPACITY — the range max_a θ_ra − min_a θ_ra. Certifying means excluding every alternative that would change the answer, so the design's value is the cheapest such alternative.

Three quantities must be kept distinct. J_scalar is the pair-flip value computed at the CURRENT extrema with ordering constraints dropped; J_old is the quadratic programme inside the current-extrema region; J_full is the infimum over the whole alternative set, with the extrema free in either relation. By inclusion of feasible sets:

and there is NO general order between J_scalar and J_full. Allocators are routinely built on J_scalar because it is cheap. This work asks what that costs when the extrema can move — and the answer is that it costs everything, in both directions.
II.  Contributions

C1.  THE SCALAR PROXY IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BY NO CONSTANT. We construct two explicit two-relation, three-action families. In the first the ratio J_full/J_scalar is driven to 0; in the second it is driven to +∞. Both are exact-arithmetic constructions with explicit feasible alternatives and elementary lower bounds — no optimiser, no sampled world, no seed. Hence no constant correction can repair the proxy.

C2.  THE TRUE ALTERNATIVE SET IS A FINITE UNION OF CONVEX PAIR REGIONS. We prove a finite max/min set identity on the real RANGE target, not a Top-1 surrogate, with the extrema chosen from the ALTERNATIVE and never frozen at truth. Each region is convex with no definiteness assumption on any observation matrix.

C3.  THE ENERGY ORACLE BECOMES A FINITE CHECK. A number lower-bounds the energy over the whole alternative set if and only if it does so on every pair region, so certifying is a finite conjunction of convex problems and no infimum over an infinite-dimensional set is ever taken.

C4.  SHRINK AND EXPAND, AS EQUIVALENCES. Range ≤ z iff all cells lie in a common interval of length z, minimised coordinate-wise by the clamp; range ≥ z iff some ORDERED pair is separated by at least z, so no third cell has to move. Both directions are equivalences, so nothing is relaxed.

C5.  AN OPTIMALITY CERTIFICATE THAT NEEDS NO MATRIX INVERSE. The textbook dual requires M invertible. We prove optimality from primal feasibility, dual non-negativity, stationarity and complementary slackness using only symmetry and positive SEMIdefiniteness, so a singular information matrix costs no extra hypothesis and no pseudoinverse.

C6.  THE SETUP-COST LAW, WITH INFEASIBILITY REPORTED AS INFEASIBILITY. An infeasible configuration has NO value and is never clamped to a small positive one; the crossing budget between two supports is derived, and when the two values are only bracketed we prove both orders remain consistent, so the honest output is UNDECIDED.
III.  Methodology
STEP 1 — THE FINITE MAX/MIN SET IDENTITY  (C2).   range_ge_iff_exists_pair

HOW IT IS CLOSED. Forward, choose a maximiser and a minimiser of the challenger relation. Backward, its range is at least the chosen difference, which dominates every pair difference in the incumbent; taking a maximum over the incumbent's pairs gives the claim. This is the model bridge, and it is the step that makes everything else possible.
STEP 2 — THE ALTERNATIVE AS A UNION OF POLYHEDRA  (C2).   alternative_union_polyhedra, pairRegion_convex
WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM STEP 1. Step 1 turns a statement about extrema into a statement about a pair, and a pair defines a polyhedron:
HOW IT IS CLOSED. Convexity of each region is checked directly on the defining inequalities, with no assumption on M.
STEP 3 — THE ORACLE IS A FINITE CHECK  (C3).   energy_lower_bound_iff, energy_ge_of_pairwise
WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM STEP 2. The union is over a finite index set, so a bound on each piece is a bound on the union — and, by Step 1, conversely.
STEP 4 — SHRINK AND EXPAND  (C4).   range_le_iff_exists_interval, range_ge_iff_exists_pair_ge, clamp_dist_le, expand_lower

HOW THEY ARE CLOSED. Shrink: the clamp into the interval is at least as close to the target as any feasible point, proved by cases on where the target lies, and the per-cell costs then sum. Expand: minimising a separable quadratic under ONE linear constraint, with the minimiser exhibited so the value is exact.
STEP 5 — THE INNER QP IN CLOSED FORM.   inner_qp_lower, inner_qp_attained

HOW IT IS CLOSED. Completing the square against the explicit minimiser. No optimiser and no multiplier theorem; the harmonic denominator is exactly the pairV shape, derived here for the range target rather than transported from the Top-1 surrogate.
STEP 6 — THE CERTIFICATE, WITHOUT AN INVERSE  (C5).   kkt_certificate, certificate_gives_lower_bound

HOW IT IS CLOSED. Expand the quadratic at the competitor, write the cross term using stationarity, and observe it equals minus the dual value at the competitor — which is non-negative because the multipliers are non-negative and the competitor is feasible. The remaining term is non-negative by positive semidefiniteness. No inverse appears anywhere.
DIRECTIONS. A lower bound for EVERY region, then their minimum, lower-bounds J. A single feasible alternative only UPPER-bounds it. The two are never conflated.
STEP 7 — FAMILY 1: THE PROXY OVERSTATES  (C1).   scalar_not_upper_to_any_constant

Two relations, three actions, Top-1 is relation i, with 0 < η ≤ 1: θ_i = (0, 1, ½), α_i = (1, 1, 1); θ_j = (0, ½, ¼), α_j = (1, 1, η). Raising ONLY the third cell of j from ¼ to 1 equalises the two capacities at cost 9η/32, while the scalar proxy reports 1/32:

θ_i = (0, 1, ¾), α_i = (1, η, 1); θ_j = (0, ½, ¼), α_j = (1, 1, 1). For ANY capacity-inverting alternative pick z between the two new capacities. Shrinking i below z costs at least [¾−z]₊²/4, opening j above z at least [z−½]₊²/4, and the two positive parts always sum to at least ¼:

HOW BOTH ARE CLOSED. One side is an explicit feasible alternative whose energy is computed; the other is an elementary lower bound holding for every alternative in the class. The positive-parts inequality is proved by three cases on z.

STEP 10 — THE BREAK-EVEN, WITHOUT THE FOLKLORE 4.   scalar_split_optimal, breakeven_iff, breakeven_not_four
The number 4 is the value of (σ_a+σ_b)² at unit variances and nothing more. With several alternatives the scalar design shares cells and the pairwise threshold does not transfer.
IV.  Results

THE TWO FAMILIES SEPARATE WITHOUT LIMIT. As η → 0 the first family drives the ratio to zero and the second to infinity. Both curves are PROVED bounds in exact arithmetic, not sampled points, so the failure of the proxy is a theorem rather than an observation.

ON THE MAIN PANEL, C_lucb IS THE BASELINE TO BEAT. Over 1000 paired instances, C_lucb certifies 797 worlds at median 20,996 queries; C_anytime 749 at 29,884; uniform 605 at 74,252. Where both certify, C_lucb is strictly faster in 748, ties 1 and loses 0, with 48 further worlds it certifies alone. This is a result ON THIS PANEL and not a domination theorem.
Fig. 1.  The two families. Family 1 forces the ratio below 9η, family 2 above (1+3η)/(16η). Both are proved bounds in exact arithmetic.
Fig. 2.  The main panel, 1000 paired instances. A result on this panel under this generator, not a domination theorem.
V.  Discussion

The two families settle a methodological question rather than a numerical one. Because the proxy errs in both directions without a constant, no calibration of it can be safe: an allocator that trusts it may either waste budget excluding an alternative that is already cheap, or stop early against one that is far cheaper than it believes. The correct object is the union of pair regions, and Step 3 shows that object is no harder to certify — it is a finite conjunction of convex problems.

Step 6 matters for practice as much as for rigour: information matrices at sparse allocations are routinely singular, and a certificate that survives singularity without a pseudoinverse is what makes the oracle usable at the boundary of the design simplex.

SCOPE — WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The DECOMPOSITION step is not formalised: that two relations occupy disjoint blocks while every other relation stays at zero cost is a model statement, and the full oracle equality is not assembled. Free response table, known variance, positive precision; under realizability coupling the cost does not separate. The certificate is SUFFICIENCY — it does not say every optimal point has one. Only weak duality is proved, so a gap is not excluded. No allocator built on this oracle has yet been compared against C_lucb.
VI.  Conclusions

When the extrema can move, the scalar pair-flip proxy is a bound in neither direction, and no constant repairs it. The true alternative set is a finite union of convex pair regions on the real range target; its energy oracle is a finite conjunction of convex problems; the inner problem has a closed form; and its optimality certificate needs no matrix inverse, so a singular information matrix costs nothing extra.
